review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting review by a Latinist. House style: simple Church Latin, spelled without macrons, with u/v and i/j as in Stage 0 (v and i only); present tense, with a few perfects (venit, vidit, fuit, dixit) in the last units.

english.source: drafted with the text; not reviewed

sentences.text: Martha in domo parva habitat. Domus bona est.
sentences.english: Martha lives in a small house. The house is good.

sentences.text: Hodie Samuel in domo Marthae est. Libenter in domo est.
sentences.english: Today Samuel is in Martha's house. He is gladly in the house.

sentences.text: Salve, Martha! Domus tua bona est.
sentences.english: Hello, Martha! Your house is good.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Salve, Samuel! Domus mea parva est, sed domum meam amo.
sentences.english: Hello, Samuel! My house is small, but I love my house.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Ecce porta! Porta magna est.
sentences.english: Look, a door! The door is big.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Porta magna est, sed fenestra parva est. Ecce fenestra!
sentences.english: The door is big, but the window is small. Look, the window!
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Fenestram video. Portam quoque video.
sentences.english: I see the window. I see the door too.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Et quid in mensa vides?
sentences.english: And what do you see on the table?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: In mensa video panem et lac.
sentences.english: On the table I see bread and milk.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Mensam amo. Panem et lac habeo. Multa in domo habeo.
sentences.english: I love the table. I have bread and milk. I have many things in the house.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Multa habes! Libenter in domo tua sum.
sentences.english: You have many things! I am gladly in your house.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Et tu, Samuel? Ubi habitas?
sentences.english: And you, Samuel? Where do you live?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: In domo parva habito. Domus mea magna non est.
sentences.english: I live in a small house. My house is not big.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Domus tua et domus mea bonae sunt. Bene est!
sentences.english: Your house and my house are good. It is well!
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Libenter te video, Martha. Domum tuam amo.
sentences.english: I am glad to see you, Martha. I love your house.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Gratias tibi ago, Samuel. Lac bibis? Lac bonum est.
sentences.english: Thank you, Samuel. Do you drink milk? The milk is good.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Lac volo. Gratias tibi ago. Multa habes, et multa mihi das.
sentences.english: I want milk. Thank you. You have many things, and you give me many.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Anna quoque in domo Marthae est.
sentences.english: Anna is in Martha's house too.

sentences.text: Salve, Martha! Salve, Samuel! Quomodo valetis?
sentences.english: Hello, Martha! Hello, Samuel! How are you?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Bene valemus, Anna. Et tu? Quomodo vales?
sentences.english: We are well, Anna. And you? How are you?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Bene valeo, sed fessa sum. Ubi est frater meus?
sentences.english: I am well, but I am tired. Where is my brother?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Lucius in schola est. Magister bonus est.
sentences.english: Lucius is at school. He is a good teacher.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Et Marcus? Estne in schola?
sentences.english: And Marcus? Is he at school?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Non est in schola. Hic est, in domo mea. Marcus clavem non habet.
sentences.english: He is not at school. He is here, in my house. Marcus does not have his key.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Ubi est clavis? Estne in mensa?
sentences.english: Where is the key? Is it on the table?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Non est in mensa. Marcus clavem non habet.
sentences.english: It is not on the table. Marcus does not have the key.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Marcus quoque in domo est. Puer bonus est, sed clavem non habet.
sentences.english: Marcus is in the house too. He is a good boy, but he does not have the key.

sentences.text: Salve, Anna! Ubi est clavis mea? Clavem non habeo.
sentences.english: Hello, Anna! Where is my key? I do not have the key.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Clavis tua hic est, Marce. Ecce clavis!
sentences.english: Your key is here, Marcus. Look, the key!
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Gratias tibi ago! Clavem habeo. Et lac volo.
sentences.english: Thank you! I have the key. And I want milk.
sentences.speaker: nico
